posts.text: WarTranslated Two Russian missiles and a jet drone fell in Poland during Russia's massive attack on Ukraine, Defense Minister Kosiniak-Kamysz says. He calls it another provocation. Polish military logged 11 air targets in total that could have violated the country's airspace, he adds. https://twitter.com/wartranslated/status/2123729802976698598/photo/1 Monitoring channels say a cruise missile crossed into Polish airspace this morning. Poland's army says it got word of a suspected violation by unidentified air objects and is now checking radar data. Poland's Operational Command says an object probably came down near Chmielek in Bilgoraj county, PAP reports. Online reports say CCTV caught an explosion there, about 46 km from the Ukrainian border. Polish authorities have not officially reported it. Tusk says he received reports from ministers Kosiniak-Kamysz and Kierwinski. There is no air threat for now, and services are working at the site, he says. - WarTranslated tweet

Status-6 #UPDATE : Polish Minister of National Defence Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz now says that THREE Russian aerial objects have penetrated the Polish airspace and fell on the territory of Poland this morning. He confirmed that the one near Nowy Lipowiec was a Kh-101 cruise missile, while adding that another missile (likely also Kh-101) fell near the town of Rudnik nad Sanem in Subcarpathian Voivodeship. Kosiniak-Kamysz also reported that a Russian jet-powered drone (presumably Geran-4) went down in the area of the village of Mołodycz in Subcarpathian Voivodeship. Below a map showing approximate locations of the three fallen objects. On November 20, 2026, at around 6:30 a.m. local time, an aerial object believed to be a Russian Kh-101 air-launched cruise missile impacted a field in the vicinity of the settlement of Nowy Lipowiec, Lublin Voivodeship, in eastern Poland. The incident occurred during a large-scale Russian missile and drone attack on Ukraine, involving roughly 80 cruise missiles, up to 20 ballistic missiles, and about 400 drones. Polish authorities have already reacted to the event, with Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk confirming that there was a violation of Polish airspace and informing the public that relevant services were already working at the scene of the explosion. Notably, the explosion occurred just 70km away from the Nowa Dęba training ground, a major Polish military training area in southeastern Poland's Podkarpackie Voivodeship. Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in February 2022, Polish airspace has been violated multiple times by Russian munitions and aircraft. The most notable incidents included the fall of a Kh-55 cruise missile 450km deep inside Poland in December 2022, a mass incursion by Gerbera long-range UAVs in September 2025, as well as the impact of a Kh-101 cruise missile in Lublin Voivodeship in July 2026. - Status-6 tweet

Visioner BIG | 🇺🇦 🔥 🇷🇺 ‼️ ‼️ A combined Ukrainian missile and drone strike reportedly hit the headquarters of Russia’s 58th Combined Arms Army in occupied Berdiansk on November 18, killing seven Russian servicemen and wounding 12 others. According to the Russian military-linked Telegram channel Dosye Shpiona, those killed included the 58th Army’s personnel department chief and Sergei Kosobokov, son of Lieutenant General Mikhail Kosobokov, commander of Russia’s 49th Combined Arms Army. The reported casualties and identities have not been independently verified. The 58th Army also participated in Russia’s 2008 war against Georgia and is now deployed in Ukraine. 🔥 A successful strike on an army headquarters could disrupt command coordination and personnel management beyond the immediate casualties. The reported attack also carries historical significance, targeting a Russian formation involved in the invasion of Georgia and now fighting in Ukraine. tweet
